entries.org: Purdue University, School of Mechanical Engineering and School of Science
entries.role: B.S. Mechanical Engineering; B.S. Applied Statistics; Minor in Economics

bullets: Mapping impacts onto Atlas’s mesh with encoders and forward kinematics, estimating impact energy from Khatib’s operational-space effective mass and an OLS velocity fit; building a physics-based MuJoCo impact simulation.

Building an impact forensics pipeline and Flask/Plotly dashboard on a Linux VM over ~28k impact events from ~900 test logs: ETL into SQLite, a 3D impact heatmap, and per-event waveforms used by engineers during testing.
Modeling hardware thermal behavior in Python, using Savitzky-Golay filtering and multi-start least squares to predict steady-state temperatures across hundreds of units without full-length tests.
Built LSTM/XGBoost forecasts of daily paint use with Monte Carlo intervals, achieving a 4.7% material reduction.

entries.org: Chortos Lab – Soft Adaptive Systems and Structures
bullets: Wrote a Python computer-vision tracker and LabVIEW/MATLAB data acquisition to measure gel samples, and used them to formulate gels with over 50% more force output.
Designed and CNC-machined a valve spring canister in Creo with GD&T drawings; ran UL 429 solenoid valve tests.

entries.org: Legged Robot State Estimation and Control
bullets: Built a contact-aided error-state Kalman filter in C++ for a simulated Unitree Go1, fusing IMU and leg kinematics to 0.013 m/s velocity error, against 1.38 m/s for the IMU alone.
Verified it with GoogleTest (finite-difference Jacobian checks, parity with a Python reference) and an observability analysis of what the sensors can and can’t see.
Stress-tested it under foot slip and contact latency, and fixed the latency and weak-tilt-observability failures.
Closed the loop in Python simulation with no falls, and added an MIT Cheetah 3-style QP balance controller.

Designed a 1 kHz PI motor velocity controller in C++ for an ESP32-S3, tuned from a motor model with feed-forward and anti-windup, and verified it in co-simulation with a model of the motor and forearm.
Wrote the FreeRTOS firmware with fault monitors, a watchdog, and a kill switch, tested with GoogleTest in CI.
Cut simulated EMG-to-motion latency from 103 to 43 ms on real EMG via new signal processing and loop tuning.
Led the 5-engineer electronics team and redesigned the EMG board schematic in KiCad, raising cross-day gesture decoding from 31% to 87% in emulation.
